fact_text: Pakistani bank earnings rest almost entirely on retail deposits: borrowing from the State Bank or another institution to on-lend leaves a very thin spread, and investment banking is negligible.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst models every bank as percentages of deposits - net spread, non-interest income, operating cost of running the branch network, and provisions - then sums them to a pre-tax return on deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banks lend to the Government of Pakistan at roughly the policy rate and to other businesses at around a percentage point above it, so the main driver of net spread is the cost of deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because deposit cost dominates spread, the share of current accounts in total deposits and the rate paid on savings accounts are the two variables that decide which bank earns most.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Conventional banks in Pakistan must pay savings account holders at least the policy rate minus 1.5 percentage points, a minimum deposit rate requirement from which Islamic banks were long exempt.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst converts return on deposits into return on capital by multiplying by about ten, since roughly PKR 100 billion of capital is needed to run PKR 1,000 billion of deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Of the roughly PKR 100 billion of capital behind PKR 1,000 billion of deposits, about PKR 60 billion sits with the State Bank as non-earning reserves and PKR 30-40 billion is branch and systems infrastructure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A bank is a leveraged product: with capital of one rupee against a hundred rupees of loans, losing even a small fraction of the loan book can wipe out the institution, so provisioning behaviour is decisive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues a high price-to-book multiple for a high-return bank is justified, and that banks looking cheap on book value are usually cheap because of a fundamental flaw in their profit-making ability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The State Bank exempted deposits of financial institutions from the conventional minimum deposit rate, which stops mutual-fund money arbitraging into bank savings accounts when rates fall quickly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A moderate minimum deposit rule was extended to Islamic banks: they must share 75 percent of gross return on financing with individual savings account holders, with institutional deposits exempt.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst calculates that with long-run rates near 11-12 percent, the new rule obliges Islamic banks to pay savers roughly 9 to 9.5 percent versus over 10 percent for conventional banks, narrowing but not removing their funding advantage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes Meezan Bank was the only Islamic bank paying savers less than the new 75 percent threshold, thanks to the strength of its deposit franchise, so the rule change bites it hardest.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's key thing to watch as rates fall is which banks raise their current account share, since the bulk of banking sector profit comes from non-remunerative deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Falling rates cut bank earnings in principle but the analyst sees them as net positive for minority shareholders, because the market awards a higher multiple as the discount rate on future profits falls.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lower interest rates reduce Pakistan's debt-to-GDP and therefore the risk of local debt restructuring, which is the single largest tail risk for banks given their huge sovereign exposure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst illustrates the restructuring risk with a bank worth PKR 200 billion holding PKR 1,000 billion of government loans: a 10 percent haircut alone could halve its market capitalisation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Banking Sector' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: National Foods holds over 50 percent market share in four separate categories - recipe mixes, pickles, jams and ketchup - which the analyst treats as a durable advantage because consumer taste is hard to shift once formed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Three products generate about 90 percent of revenue: recipe mixes and spices at 40-50 percent, tomato ketchup at 20-25 percent and pickles at roughly 15 percent.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Raw materials are agricultural, with imported tomato paste - mostly from China - the single largest input, alongside packaging and advertising as the other major cost lines.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Import restrictions in 2023 and 2024 pushed the company to localise, and it now has a farmer-collaboration plan to produce about 8,000 tons of tomato paste from locally grown tomatoes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The company spent about PKR 1.5 billion on transport in FY24 because its factory was in Karachi while roughly 70 percent of Pakistan's population lives in Punjab and the north.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A one million square foot plant in the Faisalabad special economic zone began commercial operations in February 2024, cutting transport cost by up to 50 percent and exempting the company from 39 percent income tax including super tax for ten years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Faisalabad plant cost roughly PKR 7 billion and the tax exemption alone is expected to save about PKR 1.5-2 billion a year, with the transport savings on top.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Production for northern Pakistan has moved to Faisalabad, leaving the old Karachi plant to serve Karachi demand and manufacture export volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the budget applied normal taxation to exporters, the company set up a UAE subsidiary to handle its export business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The company's Canadian subsidiary A1 Cash and Carry runs eight wholesale retail stores built over five to six years, each averaging about CAD 30-35 million of annual sales, with one or two new stores a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cash and carry wholesale retail is a stable business earning roughly 5 to 6 percent net margin, which the analyst says describes the A1 subsidiary's economics.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst insists on never valuing consolidated accounts when a group contains fundamentally different businesses, and instead values each separately before adding them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst models FY26 local revenue near PKR 50 billion, gross profit of PKR 15-20 billion, profit before tax of PKR 4-5 billion and, with Faisalabad production untaxed, profit after tax of PKR 3-4 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Applying a 20 times multiple to the local FMCG business the analyst gets about PKR 60-70 billion of value, on the grounds that local FMCG is not capital intensive and the long-term record is strong.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values A1 Cash and Carry at PKR 60 billion on FY26 revenue of about PKR 60 billion and profit after tax near PKR 3 billion, then takes 60 percent for the ownership stake and discounts a further 25 percent for dividend repatriation tax, reaching roughly PKR 27 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dividends received in Pakistan from a foreign subsidiary attract about 25 percent tax - 15 percent dividend tax plus 10 percent super tax - which the analyst applies as a discount when valuing overseas subsidiaries.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Adding the two businesses, the analyst arrives at a combined value of roughly PKR 95-100 billion, or about PKR 450 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sales and profits peak in the Ramadan quarter and in summer quarters, so weaker winter quarters are normal and full-year rather than quarterly figures should be used to estimate earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Following Peter Lynch, the analyst treats heavy sponsor buying as a stronger signal than selling, since insiders sell for many reasons but buy only when they judge their own company the best option on their radar.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst warns the sponsor-buying signal is gameable in small Pakistani companies, where operators accumulate through benami accounts and add token director purchases late to attract retail buyers before exiting, so quantity and company type matter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because bonus shares became taxable in Pakistan, listed companies have shifted towards share splits instead as the way to adjust share price levels.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'All you need to know about National Foods - Pakistan's best local FMCG company.' (YouTube transcript, undated)
